the γ-gauche effects in diselenogermane derivatives are larger than the corresponding γ-gauche interactions in monoselenogermanes, and that they are also larger than the γ-gauches in diselenides.

a systematic study of the 77Se NQR spectra of the Se–Ge–C–C system in order to evaluate the steric compression effect of a γ-carbon atom on the 77Se chemical shieldings.
the study of the γ-effect of the γ-C(γ) atom in mono- and diorganogermanes, which is a very rare example of a γ-effect on 77Se NQR chemical shift.
the synthesis and the structural characterization (by X-ray diffraction, NMR, and DFT calculations) of a novel class of organoselenium compounds.

the 77Se N-chemical shift is a very sensitive probe of the γ-gauche interactions.

the γ-gauche interaction is a steric compression effect that is not a function of the nature of the group bonded to the γ carbon, but it is a function of the steric hindrance exerted by the γ-carbon on the Se–Ge bond.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the γ-gauche interaction is a strong and significant effect.
, the steric compression effect of γ-carbon is not a constant but it depends on the nature of the substituents on the germanium atom.
the γ-carbon atom is the most efficient in the steric compression of selenium in the Se–X(α)–Y(β)–Z(γ) system (X, Y, Z = C, Ge).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 77Se chemical shielding is very sensitive to the γ-effect and the 77Se-NQR spectroscopy is a powerful tool to detect it.
the γ-gauche effects are not only sensitive to the nature of substituents at the γ-carbon but also depend on the number and the nature of the substituents at α-carbon.
